title: Rename 'util time-ms' → 'util timestamp' and 'util time-now' → 'util now'
description: Rename 'util time-ms' to 'util timestamp' and 'util time-now' to 'util now'. Both old names are opaque ('time-ms' leaks the implementation detail that it returns milliseconds) or inconsistent with common conventions. Keep the old names as deprecated aliases.
prerequisiteState: Stories 1–27 complete. Commands registered as 'util time-ms' and 'util time-now'. The uuid command is unchanged and remains as-is.
goal: After this story: 'zapi util timestamp' returns epoch milliseconds as { "ts": 1742256000000 }. 'zapi util now' returns the formatted time string as { "now": "20/03/26 21:15:30.427" }. Old names 'util time-ms' and 'util time-now' still work with deprecation warnings.
scope: In src/ZapiCli/Commands/UtilCommands.cs: rename class 'UtilTimeMsCommand' → 'UtilTimestampCommand'. Rename 'UtilTimeNowCommand' → 'UtilNowCommand'. Update Settings class names analogously. Keep the 'UtilUuidCommand' class unchanged.
In src/ZapiCli/Program.cs, inside the 'util' branch: change AddCommand registrations from 'time-ms'/'time-now' to 'timestamp'/'now'. Keep 'uuid' unchanged.

Register deprecated shims: 'UtilTimeMsDeprecatedCommand' calling DeprecationHelper.Warn("util time-ms", "util timestamp") and 'UtilTimeNowDeprecatedCommand' calling DeprecationHelper.Warn("util time-now", "util now"). Register under the old names 'time-ms' and 'time-now' in the util branch.
Do NOT change the output JSON fields or format: 'util timestamp' still outputs { "ts": <epoch_ms> } and 'util now' still outputs { "now": "<formatted_time>" }.
acceptanceCriteria: 'zapi util timestamp' outputs { "ts": <epoch_ms> } — same JSON as old 'util time-ms'
'zapi util now' outputs { "now": "<formatted>" } — same JSON as old 'util time-now'
'zapi util time-ms' still works with a deprecation warning
'zapi util time-now' still works with a deprecation warning
contextForAgent: This is the same pattern as story 32 — straightforward class rename + deprecated shim. Read UtilCommands.cs to confirm the class structure. Confirm the output JSON key names (ts vs timestamp vs milliseconds) by reading the current implementation — do NOT change the JSON key names, only the command names.
